key_insight: Introducing DOMINO, a large-scale dataset and benchmark that enables spatiotemporal learning for Vision–Language–Action models, showing that multi-frame temporal reasoning is essential for robust robotic manipulation in dynamic, moving-target environments.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of dynamic manipulation data and the limitation of single-frame VLA models, which prevents generalization to tasks with moving objects and changing scenes.
method: Curate DOMINO: 35 manipulation tasks with hierarchical difficulty levels and diverse dynamic scenarios to train and evaluate models.
Move beyond single-frame inputs by framing problems as spatiotemporal sequences (multi-frame / video inputs) for action grounding.
Provide a standardized benchmark and baseline evaluations to measure generalization and temporal reasoning performance.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to develop and benchmark models that generalize to real-world, time-varying manipulation tasks, accelerating progress in robust robot behavior under dynamic conditions.
visual_elements: Dataset overview infographic: task grid showing 35 tasks with icons for hierarchical difficulty and moving-target annotations
Timeline / sequence diagram: multi-frame input → temporal encoder → action output to illustrate spatiotemporal reasoning
Benchmark comparison bar chart: single-frame vs multi-frame performance across task difficulty levels
Example sequence panels: robot interacting with a moving object (before, during, after) to highlight dynamic challenges
paper_title: Towards Generalizable Robotic Manipulation in Dynamic Environments
paper_authors: Heng Fang, Shangru Li, Shuhan Wang, Xuanyang Xi, Dingkang Liang
